prompt: Plan credential rotation for a service fleet that uses one database credential and two third-party API credentials. Today the values are copied into CI variables and long-lived process environments; some replicas restart only weekly, one batch worker can be offline for hours, and operators have no authoritative consumer inventory. Move delivery to workload identity or a managed secret service where supported, build a complete consumer/version inventory, design a staged rotation that can tolerate overlapping old/new values only for a bounded period, verify every consumer has switched, revoke the old credentials, and define rollback/emergency compromise behavior plus audit. Keep end-user login credentials out of scope.

requirements: API/worker/batch service consumers with staggered restart/offline behavior
database and vendor credential stores supporting controlled old/new overlap
access/audit logs showing which credential version each consumer uses

falsifiableChecks.assertion: The plan identifies every service/replica/batch consumer and current credential version before rotation, including offline/stale consumers rather than assuming deployment completion implies credential adoption.
New credentials are delivered through a managed secret/workload identity path that avoids source control, CI plaintext variables, command-line exposure, broad process inheritance, and ordinary logs.
Rotation uses the provider/database-supported overlap or staged cutover with an explicit deadline, verifies successful use of the new version for every consumer, and only then revokes the old value.
Rollback has a bounded path that restores service without leaving both credentials accepted indefinitely or reintroducing an untracked legacy secret.

Emergency compromise response can bypass the normal leisurely rotation cadence, revoke the affected credential, identify impacted consumers/data, reissue safely, and preserve administrative/use audit evidence.
